anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, the two M12 CAN connectors J5 ('CAN Interface A') and J4 ('CAN Interface B') are wired to the SAME signal nets on the same pin numbers: pin2=NET0195, pin3=NET0169, pin5=NET0006 (only pin1 differs, NET0206 vs NET0063). Thus the CAN data lines of the two interfaces are merged onto one set of nets.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes 'two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 and J13', i.e. each connector must carry its own separate, isolated CAN differential pair.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet (tile 10): J5 'CAN Interface A' pins 2/3/5 = NET0195/NET0169/NET0006; J4 'CAN Interface B' pins 2/3/5 = NET0195/NET0169/NET0006
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 and J13

anomalies.impact: The two intended independent, isolated CAN buses are shorted together at the connectors; Odrive controllers wired to 'A' and 'B' would share one bus, defeating isolation and causing address/traffic collisions between the two motor groups.

anomalies.observed: The shared I2C bus (NET0062/NET0155) is pulled up to two different 3.3 V rails: R26/R35 (10 k) tie SDA/SCL to 3.3V_PI_OUT (the CM4's Pi 3.3 V, also U57's VDD), while R46 (5.1 k) ties the same SDA/SCL nets to +3V3 (the external switched regulator). This joins the two nominally-separate 3.3 V supplies through the pull-up network.
anomalies.expected: The board's own note states the rails are deliberately separate ('+3.3V - switched 3.3v regulator ... 3.3V_PI_OUT - always on 3.3v from pi ... we use an external 3.3v regulator because the Pi's onboard 3.3v regulator can fail if shorted, so we use it as little as possible'); a shared I2C bus should be pulled up to a single always-on rail to avoid back-feeding the Pi 3.3 V into the external rail (and vice-versa) when one supply is off.

evidence.quote: CM4 sheet (tile 1): R26, R35 = 10K between NET0155/NET0062 and 3.3V_PI_OUT; Motion Sensing sheet (tile 6): R46 = 5.1k between NET0155/NET0062 and +3V3

3.3V_PI_OUT - always on 3.3v from pi, for GPIO expander; +3.3V - switched 3.3v regulator ... we use an external 3.3v regulator because the Pi's onboard 3.3v regulator can fail if shorted, so we use it as little as possible

anomalies.impact: When the external 3.3 V regulator is disabled, the Pi's 3.3 V back-feeds the external rail through the I2C pull-ups and the I2C pins of unpowered sensors, risking latch-up and fighting between the two regulators.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the intended architecture in two places: the two CAN interface connectors share the same CAN signal nets (merging the supposedly isolated CAN0/CAN1 buses), and the common I2C bus is pulled up to both the external +3V3 and the CM4's 3.3V_PI_OUT rails, joining two supplies the design explicitly keeps separate. The 16 MHz CAN crystals and other documented known-issues match the spec and are not flagged.
